Re:     Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C., Docket No. CP26-540-000
        South Texas Enhancement Project
        Supplemental Filing – Pipeline Route Modification

Dear Ms. Reese:

        On June 5, 2026, Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C. (“TGP”) filed a certificate application in the
above-referenced docket seeking the issuance of a certificate of public convenience and necessity from the Federal
Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission”) for the construction and operation of the South Texas
Enhancement Project (“Project”).

         On July 8, 2026, Nanette Chapa filed comments regarding the location of the proposed Project
(Accession No. 20260708-5076). On August 13, 2026, TGP submitted a filing in response (Accession No.
20260813-5006) indicating that TGP would pursue an alternate route of the proposed Project pipeline to avoid
impacting Ms. Chapa’s property. Additionally, within TGP’s response to the August 25, 2026 Environmental
Information Request issued by the Commission (Accession No. 20260908-5303), TGP noted that a supplemental
filing containing information regarding this alternative route would be provided once all details regarding the
alternative route had been finalized, which was anticipated to occur by the end of October 2026. In accordance
with this effort, TGP submits this supplemental filing with information regarding the route modifications to the
proposed Project pipeline that have occurred since the June 5, 2026 certificate application filing for the Project.

        TGP notes that portions of this Supplemental Filing contain sensitive, privileged information.
Attachment 1 contains privileged information regarding affected landowners. Attachment 7 contains privileged
information regarding the location, nature, and character of cultural resources. TGP requests that these documents
be accorded privileged treatment, pursuant to Section 388.112 of the Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R. §
388.112 (2025), and has labeled the identified attachments as “CUI // PRIV – CONTAINS PRIVILEGED
INFORMATION – DO NOT RELEASE”.

          In accordance with the Commission’s filing requirements, TGP is submitting this filing with the
Commission’s Secretary through the eFiling system. Copies of this filing are being served on all parties on the
official service list for the above-referenced docket. Any questions concerning this filing should be addressed to
the undersigned at (205) 325-3668.
                                                Respectfully submitted,

                                               TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY, L.L.C.

                                    EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
TGP is submitting supplemental information to the application for a certificate of public convenience and
necessity that it filed on June 5, 2026 with the Commission in Docket No. CP26-540-000 for the proposed
Project. This supplemental filing provides information regarding a minor reroute of the STEP Loop, and
associated workspace adjustments and changes to existing access roads, that have occurred since the
June 5, 2026 certificate application filing for the Project. Updates regarding these revisions to the Project
scope, including updates to the June 5, 2026 Environmental Report for the Project to reflect such Project
scope changes, are discussed below and provided in the attachments to this supplemental filing. The
updates discussed herein are being undertaken primarily to accommodate a landowner’s request to reroute
the proposed STEP Loop around her property. As further discussed herein, the proposed reroute has been
reviewed by TGP and TGP has determined that the reroute would not materially change the environmental
impacts that would be associated with the Project.
For this supplemental filing, narrative and table updates that appear in red, bold, and italic text indicate
information that has been updated to reflect current Project information. Information reflected in red
strikethrough text indicates information that has been removed to reflect current Project information.
Information that is not updated in this supplemental filing remains correct per the original filing.

This shift required several ATWS near the southern extent of the STEP Loop and surrounding the OPP
Facility to be altered. In addition, existing access road STEP-PAR-04 will no longer be needed for
construction due to the proposed reroute. These updates, identified below, are depicted on the updated
alignment sheets and Project figures that are provided in Attachment 3. The proposed reroute would not

Section 6.3 Mineral Resources: Texas’ mineral resources include both fuel and non-fuel mineral production
throughout the state. Texas’ fuel-based mineral resources include oil, natural gas, and lignite, which are
currently being recovered in the state. Texas’ non-fuel mineral resources include sand and gravel
(construction and industrial), stone (crushed and dimension), cement (masonry and portland), salt, clay
(bentonite and common), and limestone. Texas leads in cement, common clay, crushed stone, dimension
stone, and gypsum production. A variety of other industrial minerals produced in Texas include ball clay,
bentonite, construction and industrial sand and gravel, and zeolites (USGS 2026h). There are no mineral
resources within 0.25 miles of the Project area. Figure 6.A.2 illustrates the location of 53 oil and gas wells
located within 0.25 miles of the Project area. One of the wells identified was previously is located within
the Project area; however, due to the shift of the pipeline and its associated workspaces, this well is
no longer located within the STEP Loop temporary workspace, near milepost 1.4, and is a permitted
location for vertical well-boring. The well was operated by TEPPCO Crude Pipeline LLC, which has since
been acquired by Enterprise L.P. It has a total permitted depth of 300 ft below ground surface. There is no
status update since the well was hard filed with the Railroad Commission of Texas in 1999. Based on field
surveys, TGP assumes this well was never completed following the issuance of the permit. No additional
wells identified within 0.25 miles of the Project are located within the Project workspace, and 18 of the wells
identified within 0.25 miles of the Project are noted to be abandoned and either plugged or dry (The Railroad
Commission of Texas 2026). Additionally, none of these wells are visible on aerial imagery. No impacts on
these wells are anticipated during construction or operation of the Project. However, if a well is identified in
the field during construction, TGP will erect safety fencing and a 10-foot buffer surrounding the well to
minimize the potential for direct impact.

Section 7.2.2.2 Designated Farmland: All of the soil map units crossed by the STEP Loop, the OPP Facility,
the STEP Meter Stations appurtenant facilities to the aforementioned facilities, and the contractor yards in
Nueces County, Texas, are rated as prime farmland; however, two soil map units (Bn and Of) crossed by

the STEP Facilities are rated as unique farmland, farmland of statewide importance, or farmland of local

Section 7.2.2.5 Erodibility: One soil map unit (OfBn) crossed by STEP-PAR-01 in Nueces County is rated
as highly susceptible to wind erosion. All other soil map units crossed by the STEP Facilities in Nueces
County are rated as moderately susceptible to wind erosion. The one soil map unit crossed by the
Compressor Station and PAR in Brooks County is rated as highly susceptible to wind erosion (see Tables
7.2-1 and 7.2-2).
Section 7.3.3 Designated Farmland Soils: The STEP Loop, contractor yards, NET and Whistler Meter
Stations, OPP Facility, MLV and Pig trap facility, TAR, and four PARs cross soils designated as prime
farmland, and the STEP Loop, GCX and NET Meter Stations, and four PARs cross soils designated
as farmland of statewide importance. Accordingly, approximately 53.54 acres of prime farmland or
farmland of statewide importance are impacted by the Project (see Tables 7.2-1 and 7.2-2). Of this,
approximately 18.01 acres are associated with permanent facilities, while impacts to approximately 35.53
acres will be temporary and short term, limited to the construction phase (see Tables 7.2-1 and 7.2-2).
Additionally, the land for the approximately 1.54-mile-long STEP Loop (Milepost 0.0 to Milepost 1.54) is
dominated by active agricultural fields. However, no Project components cross soils designated as unique
farmland, farmland of statewide importance,or farmland of local importance. The most significant impact on
designated farmland typically occurs where agricultural practices are active. Potential impacts include soil
erosion, interference with and damage to agricultural surface and subsurface drainage systems and
irrigation systems, the mixing of topsoil and subsoil, the potential loss of fertile topsoil, and topsoil
compaction.

Section 7.3.6 Wind and Water Erosion: The Compressor Station and PARs in Brooks County and Nueces
County cross soils rated as highly susceptible to wind erosion. Accordingly, approximately 22.41 acres of
soils rated as highly susceptible to wind erosion are impacted by the Project (see Tables 7.2-1 and 7.2-2).
Of this, approximately 14.30 acres are associated with permanent facilities, while impacts to approximately
8.11 acres will be temporary and short term, limited to the construction phase (see Tables 7.2-1 and 7.2-
2).
Section 7.3.7: Stony-Rocky and Droughty Soils: Approximately 76.00 acres of the acreage impacted by the
proposed Project are rated as having droughty soils (see Tables 7.2-1 and 7.2-2). Of this, approximately
32.36 acres are associated with permanent facilities, while impacts to approximately 43.64 acres will be
temporary and short term, limited to the construction phase (see Tables 7.2-1 and 7.2-2). Droughty soils
have a surface texture of sandy loam or coarser material and are moderately well-drained to excessively
drained. As a result, droughty soils may not be able to sustain adequate moisture levels in the root zone,
and revegetation is often difficult. TGP will use applicable measures in the FERC Plan, such as using seed
mixes appropriate to local moisture conditions, implementing soil stabilization and erosion controls, and
monitoring and maintenance, to alleviate potential impacts from construction through droughty soils.
